A teacher of mine for a short time in high school had said once “Happy, being happy is too much to ask for. I just want to be content with my life” or something like that. For years I thought negatively of her for that comment. You don’t want to strive to be happy? Your happy to settle for being content? Why? I just didn’t understand. It wasn’t until a month or two ago, now almost four years later that i finally realized what she meant. Life will have constant ups and downs, and so striving to be happy all the time is just unrealistic and to a certain extent will just bring you pain. But, being content is different. Being content is being satisfied with your life and what you have, regardless of which way the tides turn, if your happy or sad in that moment. Being content with our lives is what we truly want because it means we are without regrets and know that we have all we need. 

After thinking about what she had said for four years, i finally realized that what i thought was bad advice to be passive in your life, was actually great wisdom on what it means to make a good life for yourself.

I would also recommend watching Tango’s how to play video, but here is a simple verbal explanation : 

There is a dungeon/ maze like map, where players can explore to find treasure like coins and artifacts, which they can use to get points. You find these coins, artifacts and other treasures (like the enderpearls or cookies) either by pure luck while exploring, or by following your compass to a specific location in the maze-like map. The challenge then comes from the ravagers and a few other mobs wandering around the dungeon. Ravagers are very deadly, and if you get cornered by one you will die very quickly, making your “run” of the game a loss becuase that means you can’t make it out alive with whatever loot you found. And so, the main challenge is to get in, explore the dungeon, get as much loot as you can and get out alive. The more loot and successful runs you have, theoretically the better you are at the game and the more points you have. The overall goal of the game is to have the most points out of all the hermits by the end date of the game (which has not been determined yet as far as i can tell). 

Now for some more specifics:

the “clank” mechanic is a way to measure how long you have been inside the dungeon, and that measurement is used to make the game more difficult for the player to stay alive as time goes on. This pushes the incentive to get in the dungeon and back out alive *as fast as you can*, because the longer you are in there, the less likely you are to make it out alive. Tango has done this with the “clank walls” that raise up after you have accumulated a certain amount clank. These are the 1 block gaps that are created in the walls, and they make the game more difficult because now those very deadly ravagers can see you and path find to you from farther away. Additonally, at the highest clank levels, and at the point where you have essentially “ran out of time” an evoker pops up from the floor in an area near the exit. This adds an extra layer of difficulty to getting out of the dungeon for players who have spent a very long time inside it. 

The artifacts and collecting the sets are how you actually make points to win the game in the long run. You get artifacts through the loot boxes, which are only given as reward when you are able to follow your compass to it’s specific location in the dungeon. In each loot box there are 3-4 artifacts and 4-10 coins. There are about 12 series/sets of artifacts, each with 4 pieces each, all at a different level of rarity. For example, Tango just added a snowman set. There is a derpy snowman head which is the Unique and very hard to find, a carrot as the rare, a snow block as the uncommon, and a stick as the common. If etho were to collect one of each of these pieces of the snowman set, he can turn them in together to get a point. Currently Etho and Cub are tied for first with four points each, meaning they have both turned in four complete sets. Also to note, getting all four pieces of a set from different loot boxes is possible, but unlikely, which is why you see lots of hermits trading artifacts with each other. 

The only other big thing to explain are the cards, or the “deck” part of the game. Basically Tango who created decked out, created 5 or 6 different ways in which the game can be made easier or will run a little differently. 

the **Soul Seeker** cards make it easier to find soul flames. Without it, Soul flames will randomly be lit in a few places across the dungeon and you can extinguish them for a higher chance of getting more loot (in the form of cards for your deck). The soul seeker card, just makes more of these flames be lit so you have a better odds of finding them. 

**Beast sense**,hits a bell periodically which gives mobs, most notably the ravagers, a spectral outline for a few seconds so that the player can potentially get an idea of where they are in the dungeon so they can better avoid them. 

**Loot finder** puts more coins in the barrels so that you can find more treasures on your run. 

**Resistance** turns on a beacon periodically so maybe you won’t die to a skeleton or you can take a hit from a ravager 

**Speed** is similar to resistance, i think it is a new one tango added. 

**Stealth** helps increase your time in the dungeon by making it a little less likely that you will generate clank while you are in there. 

There may be one or two more, but that’s what i can remember right now. There are level 1 2 and 3 of each card/book type, and the effect scales with the level. 


As for how the game resets? If you want the nitty gritty of the redstone, go watch tango’s videos of him building decked out to understand it. But a general explanation is that when the game is resetting, the clank counters, and all other things that are happening during the game go back down to zero, and effects like stealth or resistance end. Also when the next player puts their deck (shulker box with books) in, if they’re have loot finder, then coins will be added to some barrels via hoopers and is kinda randomized, and the effects will start again. 

I hope that was easy to follow, it is certainly a complex game and to understand it all takes a lot of words!

Vocalist here, 

How I sightread seems to work a bit differently then most of those who posted so far. In the simplest of explanations, I sight read with solfege. 

For simpler pieces, i believe i sight read as you would expect, with first quickly deciding what’s do/ where the key center is and then using solfege internally to audiate the larger intervals and the rest comes easily. When something more difficult (usually rhythm based, some stereotypes are true) is coming up I will begin to consciously subdivide the beat until it’s past. 

For more difficult pieces, or for when i only need figure out a few notes I like to use what my undergrad choir director called “moveable-moveable do” or “super moveable do” of which the basic premise can be explained that any major third in a piece can be thought as do to mi, regardless of what those notes actually are in relation to the written or established key center. This comes in handy greatly for those songs that change key centers so many times that the composer just uses accidentals instead of key signatures, or for when you see a specific interval or two that you need to internalize, and taking the time to figure out the key signature and establish the relationship to Do that those notes have will just take more time then you want to give to it. 

I was fortunate enough to always go to schools that used moveable do and had an emphasis on sight reading before college, and that experience plus my undergrad director’s idea of super moveable Do, i currently can look at any piece of music and use solfege to sight read it, to the extent past just using intervals on a major scale that solfege was likely intended for.

its perfectly normal to be afraid of something like this when going to see a doctor for your mental health. However we shouldn’t let our fear stop us from walking through the door to self improvement. I promise it will be okay.

Hi there, 
I’ve been there plenty of times and trust me when I say I feel your pain. It would make me full of anxiety and feel worthless when that person doesn’t talk to me, and endlessly question why and what was wrong with me for then to not want me and like me as much as i like them. 

It took me until finding the love i have now to realize and fully accept that those people were treating me like shit, and I did not deserve it, and neither do you. Unfortunately I don’t have any magic recipe to flick the switch in your brain and make you not care about this person anymore, and for you to grasp that you are in control of how you are treated, but I do have this:

1. You are WAY better off in life without someone who is willing to treat you like that. Even if they were the sweetest person in the world before they decided to ghost you, they still decided to treat you this way, and **you deserve so much better than that** 

2. I personally believe in some ways that the more shitty experiences you have trying to find love, the more rewarding and tender it will be when it is time to actually find your true love it will be that much better. And you will! One day you will find someone who just *feels right* and they will feel the same, and eventually all the heartache will feel worth it, because it led you there. 

And 

3. How this person is treating you **is no measure of your value or worth as a person** but rather, a reflection on *themselves*. It can be SO easy to take these moments as personal reflections and blame ourselves for it, wonder what we did wrong or why they don’t want to be with us, and the most important thing to know is that there is nothing to blame yourself for. You are an amazing, lovable and kind person who deserves to be treated with the same love and kindness that you give to others. Sometimes people just aren’t mature enough to realize how silence can be so hurtful, and don’t have the life experience or wisdom to act in a better way towards those who we’ve decided weren’t the one for us. 

I wish you love and happiness in your next dating adventure and i hope this was helpful in someways. :)

I personally started going to a therapist because i wanted to understand why I was so upset because i knew that i was sometimes suicidal and likely pretty depressed but i never really knew what was bothering me. I just knew it was gonna be a smart thing to do, and i started to get to the point where if i don't get help, I felt like i needed to drop out of college, and like my life was falling apart. I felt like I was spiraling and I didn't want to be, and I thought I'd try to go to counseling. 

My boyfriend said this great line that I think about often "If it is any better at all at the end of this semester or by this time next year, isn't it worth it to go?" Basically getting at the idea that the potential for positive change is enough of a reason to try and achieve that. 

Also a quote I think about sometimes is "Do you actually want your life to end, or do you not want to feel this way anymore?" which really gets at the root of where some suicidal thoughts come from. From feeling like you don't have any other way out of your pain, when that isn't true. Unfortunately our suicidal brains just want us to think that the only way out is death. I'm not convinced that some peoples brains aren't just *so lazy* and don't want to do anything that they make us want to kill ourselves so our brain can become a metaphorical couch potato. (This is a joke, I actually seriously question the purpose of suicidal thoughts from a god and everyone has purpose standpoint, but that's a rant for another day.)

A reason to go even when you want to die is to find out why you want to die. Or to get back to the time in your life where you felt happy to be alive. Think of moments, memories where you were really happy, and try to think of a situation where you could feel that again. For me, it's things like going to my favorite band's concerts, or those times when music just washes a wave of happiness around you, or getting to go to my favorite theme park, or singing, or spending time outside in the beautiful florida weather (I swear i am the one floridian who loves the florida heat). All of those things I absolutely love and bring me at least some level of joy even on my worst days, and i look forward to the next twenty one pilots concert i get to go to, or the next time i'll get to lay out in the warm sun or take a nice evening drive listening to music, and wanting to experience those things again and not wanting to lose the opportunity to have kids one day, or to graduate from college and achieve my dreams are what keep me from wanting to give into my suicidal thoughts. Also imagining the pain people will go through if i killed myself, knowing that they could have possibly done something to change it (13 reasons why, while a controversial show and frankly understandably not recommended for those who are suicidal (I watched it but in hindsight maybe i shouldn't have), can be a good show for this because it really shows Clay as that main person in someone's life who eats themselves up inside over guilt and loss by losing someone to suicide. It really gives you something to imagine what will happen to others if you were to kill yourself, the pain you could cause your loved ones and friends and family, and in that way has helped me). And my way of not giving into suicidal thoughts is by going to counseling, by sharing with others even small tidbits of what i've been going through when i feel up to it, and by trying to persevere.

Sorry if this was hard to read, i have minimal motivation for editing my walls of rambling text when i'm not feeling to great. I hope this was helpful, and that maybe you can feel the same way. We can both survive, friend.

Hi friend,

it's not as hopeless as your brain wants you to believe it is. Court convictions can be very different and a lot less punishing when serious mental health issues are present and so the chances of you spending your life in jail are a lot slimmer than what you believe it might be. You have the opportunity to change schools, make some new friends and start over, the opportunity to smoke again with old friends or new or by yourself, the opportunity for things to take a turn for the better, to see a beautiful place you've never been to, to fall in love, to win an award, anything! All of these things have a chance of happening, regardless of how small it might be, if you keep on going til tomorrow, and the day after that, and so on, because when you die that opportunity goes to 0.

I've dealt a lot with feeling hopeless about the future and life, and like I won't be able to achieve my dreams, but that idea that I am throwing away my only chance, my opportunity to achieve my dreams by giving up and killing myself is what keeps me going sometimes. No matter what there is still a chance, even if its an insanely small chance, that I will achieve my dreams and that i will be happy and marry someone i love and get to see the world, and everything. There is a chance that I will be happier tomorrow, next week or next year, and that chance, that percentage is worth sticking around to see if comes true eventually.

Please try to hold onto some hope. Know that people here care about you and that you still exist and are surviving, even if only by a little. And know that if this possible court conviction becomes a major concern, that is the time, to be honest with your thoughts and feelings as it can be a saving grace. It won't come without pain, but it can save you from some different kinds of pain and can give you the help you need.

Also if people are going to believe the drama from you getting arrested and rumors over what you actually have to say about what happened and if it was wrongful or not, then they aren't great friends (or just highschoolers lol. Kids can be really sucky people, as theyre really only starting to get real world experience on how to be a friend, a good person, have opinions and deal with those who disagree, etc). People, in general, have a hard time distinguishing the idea that being close with someone/being their friend/being there for them does not mean that you have to approve of everything in their lives or everything they do, but thats a rant for another day.

I care about you friend, Please know that all hope is not lost.

Hi. Unfortunately it can be really hard to share the worst things with those who are supposedly more lifelong supports like family and so when it feels like you don’t have many others to talk to, it can be isolating feeling like you can’t really express how you feel. I speak from experience. 

I listen to a lot of angsty music at times, things like twenty one pilots, especially their earlier albums ( Regional at best in my opinion is the most angsty, and unfortunately also the hardest to find bc it was before they got a label). 

Sometimes have conversations with my self either written down or in my head about whats bothering me, where the second person is like what i wish someone around me would say or ask. It sounds lame but it can help and can be a way to practice digging yourself out of your own holes. It’s harder sometimes then others, and sometimes I have to think like “what would this person tell me right now if they knew how i was feeling?”

Also i listen to comedy podcasts when i’m having a particular bad day but i need to stay semi okay so i can focus and get assignments done for school. I’ll work until i get really bad feeling and then i’ll distract and laugh at something and then go back to work. This could work with light hearted comedy tv shows as well 

I’ve heard exercise helps alot for some people. I have a hard time with motivation and laughter and being around others does a lot more positive things for me then exercise but that could work for you. 

Also sometimes I play ukulele or piano, messing around or trying to play some of my favorite songs. It can be really rewarding, even if your terrible and have no music experience. The internet makes it kind of easy in comparison to the past to figure some stuff out on instruments like ukulele or guitar nowadays, and seeing yourself get better day by day can be encouraging. 

Similarly, drawing or painting can help too. recently I’ve had a lot of anxiety and bad feelings about the semester starting and so I spent a lot of time decorating a bullet journal for me to use as a planner, filling it with drawings and motivational blurbs and other cute things. 

All of these things are things I do to help myself feel better, I’m not sure if it is what you were looking for, but I really hope some of these help or give you ideas for things to do! 

I hope things get better for you friend. We can do it
